rules.rule: Keep most weekly endurance training time below LT1/VT1; use targeted moderate/high intensity rather than threshold-heavy training every day.
rules.exceptions: Very low-volume athletes may need a higher fraction of quality work; event-specific phases can shift distribution.

rules.rule: For VO2-focused HIIT, prefer repeatable 2–5 min intervals or validated microinterval formats that accumulate substantial high-aerobic time.
rules.exceptions: Athlete preference/tolerance and sport specificity matter; do not force one format.

rules.rule: Treat FTP as a practical field metric, not a physiological truth or sole zone anchor.
rules.exceptions: FTP can remain the primary UI metric if limitations are explicit and other performance data refine prescriptions.

rules.rule: For long-event cyclists, measure performance degradation after standardized prior work as a separate durability metric.
rules.exceptions: Emerging field; protocol must be standardized before longitudinal comparison.

rules.rule: After a technical adaptation phase, prescribe heavy lower-body strength approximately 2x/week during development blocks and ~1x/week for maintenance.
rules.exceptions: Novices, injury history, older/frail users, or medical constraints require individualized loading.

rules.rule: Separate key endurance and strength sessions by several hours or days where possible when preserving explosive-strength quality matters.
rules.exceptions: Same-day stress consolidation can be useful; athlete schedule and recovery capacity matter.

rules.rule: Prescribe mobility/stretching according to ROM/comfort goals; do not make it mandatory for cycling performance.
Offer yoga as an optional flexibility/balance/wellbeing adjunct, not a primary cycling-performance intervention.
rules.exceptions: Individual preference/adherence may make yoga highly valuable even without direct performance evidence.

rules.rule: Prioritize sleep, nutrition and load management before recovery gadgets/modalities.
rules.exceptions: Specific modalities can still improve soreness/perception or suit individual preference.

rules.rule: Use multiple readiness signals and individualized trends; do not alter training from a single HRV/resting-HR value.
rules.exceptions: Acute illness symptoms override the multi-signal rule.

rules.rule: Scale carbohydrate intake during exercise to duration/intensity; use higher intakes for prolonged demanding sessions and train the gut before very high intakes.
rules.exceptions: GI tolerance, diabetes/metabolic disease and clinical nutrition needs require individual medical/dietetic guidance.

rules.rule: Do not recommend chronic energy restriction or repeated under-fuelled hard training; flag RED-S risk features.
rules.exceptions: None for safety; specialist-guided strategies may manipulate carbohydrate availability without low energy availability.

rules.rule: For priority endurance events, reduce volume about 40–60% while maintaining frequency and some intensity for roughly 7–14 days as a default.
rules.exceptions: Individual taper response and accumulated fatigue can justify shorter/longer tapers up to ~21 days.

rules.rule: After meaningful detraining, reduce historical targets and use a progressive 2–4+ week re-entry phase.
rules.exceptions: Post-illness/injury progression must respect clinical guidance.

rules.rule: Do not auto-adjust training by predicted menstrual-cycle phase; adapt to individual symptoms and repeated personal response patterns.
rules.exceptions: Clinically diagnosed conditions and individual patterns may require specific management.

rules.rule: Do not diagnose overuse pain from bike-fit formulas; consider recent load changes and symptom history and refer persistent pain.
rules.exceptions: Qualified clinician/bike fitter assessment can use detailed biomechanics in context.
